none: PAS LIN-11CBF1: Late Roman nummus reused as a pendant
contea di ritrovamento: Lincolnshire (Inghilterra e Galles)

A late Roman copper-alloy nummus of the House of Valentinian, pierced and re-used as a pendant probably in the early Anglo-Saxon period. The coin depicts the Emperor going right dragging a captive, GLORIA ROMANORVM, struck circa AD 364-78. Obverse description: Diademed, draped and cuirassed bust right. Obverse inscription: Illegible. Reverse description: The Emperor going right holding a standard and dragging a captive. Reverse inscription: [GLORIA ROMANORVM]. Mint mark: Illegible. Die axis: 12
